title: The Light Response That Survived the Block

scenes.tts: Cut a ganglion cell off from rods and cones. If it still responds to light, whose response is it?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Light Response That Survived the Block. A ganglion cell with its link to rods and cones drawn as a cut line. Question on screen: whose response is it?
scenes.narration: Cut a ganglion cell off from rods and cones. If it still responds to light, whose response is it?

scenes.tts: Here is the logic. Rods and cones reach ganglion cells through synapses. Block those synapses with drugs.
scenes.visual: Chain: rods and cones, bipolar cell, ganglion cell. A drug cloud covers the synapses; the links turn to dashed crosses.
scenes.narration: Here is the logic. Rods and cones reach ganglion cells through synapses. Block those synapses with drugs.

scenes.tts: If a ganglion cell still responds once the block is verified, the response is most likely its own.
scenes.visual: Text on screen: still responds after a verified block = the cell's own response.
scenes.narration: If a ganglion cell still responds once the block is verified, the response is most likely its own.

scenes.tts: In two thousand two, Berson, Dunn and Takao did this in rat retina.
scenes.caption: In 2002, Berson, Dunn and Takao did this in rat retina.
scenes.visual: A flat disc of retina in a dish. Label: Berson, Dunn and Takao, 2002; isolated, flat-mounted adult rat retina.
scenes.narration: In 2002, Berson, Dunn and Takao did this in rat retina.

scenes.tts: First they labelled ganglion cells from the S C N. That told them which cells project to the clock.
scenes.caption: First they labelled ganglion cells from the SCN. That told them which cells project to the clock.
scenes.visual: A dye injected into the SCN travels back along axons and marks a few ganglion cells in the retina.
scenes.narration: First they labelled ganglion cells from the SCN. That told them which cells project to the clock.

scenes.tts: Then they recorded from those labelled cells, while the blockers were applied.
scenes.visual: A recording pipette touches one labelled cell; a bath carrying blocking drugs flows across the dish.
scenes.narration: Then they recorded from those labelled cells, while the blockers were applied.

scenes.tts: Predict. Suppose the rod and cone relay were the cell's only light signal. What should the recording show after the block?
scenes.visual: A blank voltage trace under a light bar, waiting to be drawn. Text: relay only, after the block?
scenes.narration: Predict. Suppose the rod and cone relay were the cell's only light signal. What should the recording show after the block?

scenes.tts: There should be no light-evoked change. But one remained. The labelled cells still depolarized to light.
scenes.visual: The trace draws: a noisy baseline at first, not perfectly flat, then a slow rise while the light bar is on. Label: still depolarizes with synapses blocked.
scenes.narration: There should be no light-evoked change. But one remained. The labelled cells still depolarized to light.

scenes.tts: So the response was intrinsic, made within the ganglion cell itself.
scenes.visual: Label appears: intrinsic = made within the ganglion cell.
scenes.narration: So the response was intrinsic, made within the ganglion cell itself.

scenes.tts: They also recorded from a cell body removed from the retina. That is a stronger test, with no synapses left at all.
scenes.visual: A single cell body lifted out of the retina on its own, with a pipette on it.
scenes.narration: They also recorded from a cell body removed from the retina. That is a stronger test, with no synapses left at all.

scenes.tts: So one cell can give two kinds of light response. Put both on one time axis.
scenes.visual: Two traces stacked on one shared time axis, with a light bar along the bottom: on, held, then off.
scenes.narration: So one cell can give two kinds of light response. Put both on one time axis.

scenes.tts: The relayed response, from rods and cones, usually starts fast and works in dim light. It can have both brief and lasting parts.
scenes.visual: Top trace, labelled relayed from rods and cones: a quick sharp rise at light-on, then a partial decline to a sustained level while the light is still on. Labels: usually fast; sensitive; brief and lasting parts. Schematic example for one set of conditions.
scenes.narration: The relayed response, from rods and cones, usually starts fast and works in dim light. It can have both brief and lasting parts.

scenes.tts: The cell’s own response is usually slow to start and needs brighter light. It is often long-lasting, though it adapts too.
scenes.visual: Bottom trace, labelled melanopsin: a slow climb to a high level that sags only slightly while the light bar is on. Labels: usually slow; insensitive; often sustained, also adapts. Schematic example for one set of conditions.
scenes.narration: The cell’s own response is usually slow to start and needs brighter light. It is often long-lasting, though it adapts too.

scenes.tts: When the light goes off, it decays slowly. The cell stays depolarized for a while.
scenes.visual: At light-off, the bottom trace falls only gradually, still above baseline after the light bar ends.
scenes.narration: When the light goes off, it decays slowly. The cell stays depolarized for a while.

scenes.tts: In people, these cells drive the post-illumination pupil response. The pupil stays small for a while after a light goes off.
scenes.visual: An eye: light on, the pupil narrows; light off, it stays narrow for a time before widening. Label: post-illumination pupil response.
scenes.narration: In people, these cells drive the post-illumination pupil response. The pupil stays small for a while after a light goes off.

scenes.tts: Why would slow and sustained be useful? The clock and the pupil need to know how bright it is.
scenes.visual: The plateau of the melanopsin trace highlighted, beside a clock icon and a pupil icon.
scenes.narration: Why would slow and sustained be useful? The clock and the pupil need to know how bright it is.

scenes.tts: A camera must follow fast changes. A light meter needs a steady reading.
scenes.visual: Split screen: a camera following a moving edge; a light meter with a steady needle.
scenes.narration: A camera must follow fast changes. A light meter needs a steady reading.

scenes.tts: The cells that serve the clock and the pupil are mostly a type called M one. They report how bright the world is, not what is in it.
scenes.caption: The M1 cells serve the clock and the pupil. They report how bright the world is, not what is in it.
scenes.visual: Label under the light meter: mostly M1 cells, for the clock and pupil: how bright, not what.
scenes.narration: The M1 cells serve the clock and the pupil. They report how bright the world is, not what is in it.

scenes.tts: The rat response was consistent with a pigment that peaks near four hundred eighty-four nanometres. That is a rat estimate, not a human one.
scenes.caption: The rat response fitted a pigment that peaks near 484 nanometres. That is a rat estimate, not a human one.
scenes.visual: A sensitivity-against-wavelength curve with its peak marked near 484 nm. Label: rat estimate.
scenes.narration: The rat response fitted a pigment that peaks near 484 nanometres. That is a rat estimate, not a human one.

scenes.tts: In the same volume of the journal, Hattar and colleagues showed that these rat cells carried melanopsin.
scenes.visual: A labelled cell stains for melanopsin. Label: Hattar and colleagues, 2002.
scenes.narration: In the same volume of the journal, Hattar and colleagues showed that these rat cells carried melanopsin.

scenes.tts: And melanopsin-marked mouse axons reached the S C N.
scenes.caption: And melanopsin-marked mouse axons reached the SCN.
scenes.visual: Marked axons run from a mouse retina to the SCN.
scenes.narration: And melanopsin-marked mouse axons reached the SCN.

scenes.tts: A response, a pigment and a target now pointed to one set of cells. Their signature is slow, insensitive and sustained.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the melanopsin plateau trace, with three words: slow, insensitive, sustained.
scenes.narration: A response, a pigment and a target now pointed to one set of cells. Their signature is slow, insensitive and sustained.
